title: DCU shake-up: James Gunn and Peter Safran out post-merger
gist: About two months after the Paramount–Warner Bros. merger, DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down, replaced by ex-Marvel producer Jeremy Latcham, who will report to Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chairs rather than directly to the CEO. The future of their slate beyond 2028's Superman: Man of Tomorrow is unclear.

insights.claim: James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-CEOs of DC Studios about two months after the Paramount and Warner Bros. merger, and it is unclear whether they resigned or were forced out.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Signals the merged studio's new owners are reshaping franchise leadership quickly; DC slate risk rises.
insights.locator: It's barely been two months since the controversial Paramount

insights.claim: New DC Studios head Jeremy Latcham will report to Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein, whereas Gunn and Safran had unusually reported directly to Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav, implying DC's reduced autonomy within the merged company.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: DC is being folded under Skydance's film leadership — expect more centralized, fan-driven greenlighting.

insights.claim: Jeremy Latcham, a Kevin Feige protege, produced Marvel hits including Guardians of the Galaxy, Iron Man, The Avengers and Spider-Man: Homecoming before founding a production company behind Dungeons and Dragons: Honor Among Thieves.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Hiring a Marvel-pedigree producer suggests the new owners want a proven franchise-management playbook for DC.
insights.locator: Latcham has the superhero bona fides

insights.claim: The fate of Gunn and Safran's DCU slate beyond 2028's Superman: Man of Tomorrow, which is in post-production, is uncertain after their exit.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Pipeline uncertainty for one of Hollywood's biggest IP libraries could affect the merged studio's 2029+ release calendar.
insights.locator: It's unclear whether the pair chose to resign

insights.claim: HBO's DCU television output, including Peacemaker and Lanterns, has been stronger creatively than the rebooted DC films, which the author finds enjoyable but forgettable, while Clayface debuted to good reviews and solid box office.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: TV may be DC's more reliable franchise engine under new leadership.
insights.locator: DCU fans are mourning the news

insights.claim: Gunn cited the corporate nature of the role, little recovery time between projects and ADHD as challenges, and says he is relieved to return to pure filmmaking.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Creative-executive dual roles are hard to sustain; Gunn remains attached to Man of Tomorrow as director.
insights.quote: I will miss being the co-caretaker of these great characters, but I’m also incredibly relieved and excited to get back to pure filmmaking.
insights.locator: But Gunn also noted that he sometimes found the job trying

insights.claim: The author argues the DCU should move away from the connected-universe model toward standalone films not beholden to setting up future installments.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Reflects growing fatigue with shared-universe franchise strategy that may shape studio slate decisions.
insights.locator: The DCU should be in capable hands
